articles.title: Eleições nos estados e comando do Congresso: o que está por trás da reaproximação de Lula com Alcolumbre e Motta | G1
articles.standfirst: Alinhamento do presidente com cúpula do Congresso dá fôlego a pautas do governo, enquanto apoios para disputas das próximas presidências do Senado e da Câmara são desenhados.
articles.summary: Alinhamento do presidente com cúpula do Congresso dá fôlego a pautas do governo, enquanto apoios para disputas das próximas presidências do Senado e da Câmara são desenhados.
articles.body:
Após retomar diálogo mais próximo com os presidentes da Câmara dos Deputados , Hugo Motta (Republicano-PB), e do Senado , Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) conseguiu acordos para as pautas prioritárias do governo em ano eleitoral.

Para Motta e Alcolumbre, os resultados da aproximação devem vir no próximo ano. Entre os interesses que levaram à reaproximação do trio estão três eleições, ou, no caso, reeleições.

Para Lula, o avanço de pautas como as Propostas de Emenda à Constituição (PECs) do fim da escala 6x1 e da Segurança Pública e o fim da taxa das blusinhas apelam diretamente ao eleitorado em meio à sua campanha por um quarto mandato.

As propostas devem ser analisadas pelo Congresso Nacional na próxima semana.

A campanha petista já tem aproveitado os avanços nos diálogos. A possibilidade de a PEC do fim da escala 6x1 ser aprovada já é colocada nos materiais publicitários como “uma conquista histórica”.

Já para Motta, o apoio de Lula ajuda em sua campanha de reeleição como deputado federal pela Paraíba. Outro beneficiado é seu pai, Nabor Wanderley (Republicanos-PB), que tenta o Senado no mesmo estado.

Formalmente, o PT apoia somente um candidato para o Senado na Paraíba: João Azevedo (PSB). A segunda vaga na chapa de Lula está em disputa por Veneziano Vital do Rêgo (MDB) e por Nabor. O alinhamento de Lula com Motta facilita um apoio, ainda que informal, à candidatura de seu pai.

Nesse sentido, Motta entrou em acordo com Alcolumbre e Lula para votar até quarta-feira (2), a Medida Provisória (MP) que acaba com a chamada taxa das blusinhas , imposto cobrado de compras internacionais de até US$ 50.

O tema tem apelo popular e é uma prioridade para a campanha do petista.

Outro ponto central é que Motta tem a possibilidade de concorrer a mais dois anos como presidente da Câmara, caso se reeleja deputado. Para isso, precisará do apoio do campo governista — ainda mais em um cenário no qual Lula também consiga se reeleger como presidente da República.

O presidente da República, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), entre os presidentes do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP), e da Câmara dos Deputados, Hugo Motta (Republicanos- PB) — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert

Cálculo similar ao de Motta é feito por Davi Alcolumbre. O atual presidente do Senado tem direito a tentar se reeleger para o próximo biênio e assim continuar à frente do Congresso Nacional, ambição que ele não esconde de nenhum de seus colegas senadores.

O pleito de Alcolumbre é visto como legítimo por parte do Senado. No entanto, nos últimos meses, o Partido Liberal, do candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro, tem reforçado uma estratégia para levar um senador do próprio PL ao comando do Congresso.

Para o grupo bolsonarista, essa seria uma forma de conseguir avançar com pautas como o impeachment de ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF). Pelas regras atuais, somente o presidente do Senado pode dar continuidade a um pedido de processo de retirada de um ministro do STF.

A depender do resultado das eleições para senador, uma das prioridades declaradas tanto no campo da esquerda quanto no da direita bolsonarista, Alcolumbre pode enfrentar maior resistência para conseguir se manter na cúpula do Senado.

As eleições para os presidentes do Congresso serão realizadas em fevereiro de 2027.

O fortalecimento da relação de Lula com Hugo Motta começou há meses. Um desses momentos foi justamente o avanço do fim da 6x1 na Câmara, ainda em maio deste ano. Os detalhes da proposta foram negociados diretamente entre ambos.

Outras pautas prioritárias para o governo, como a PEC da Segurança Pública, a política nacional para minerais críticos e os incentivos para a instalação de datacenters, também foram aprovadas na Câmara.

Em agosto, já durante as eleições, Lula convidou Motta para viajar com ele até o Rio Grande do Norte . Os dois viajaram no mesmo voo, no avião presidencial, e discutiram pautas de interesse do petista.

Já a reaproximação de Lula com Alcolumbre foi mais demorada e turbulenta. Os dois presidentes deixaram de se falar na época da indicação de Lula e subsequente negativa do Senado ao nome de Jorge Messias para uma vaga no STF . Foi a primeira vez que isso ocorreu desde 1894.

Depois disso, eles só voltaram a conversar em agosto . Com a campanha oficial prestes a começar, Lula e Alcolumbre se reaproximaram e, em menos de 15 dias, chegaram a acordos sobre as pautas prioritárias do governo petista.

Isso incluiu ainda a indicação de aliados de Lula para a relatoria dos projetos que estavam engavetados no Senado.

articles.title: Diferença entre deputado estadual e federal: entenda as funções | G1
articles.standfirst: Deputados estaduais fazem leis e fiscalizam os governos dos estados. Deputados federais atuam na Câmara, em Brasília, fazendo leis para o país e fiscalizando o governo federal. Série de vídeos do g1 explica os principais temas das eleições de 2026 e tira dúvidas.
articles.summary: A diferença entre deputado estadual e federal está no alcance da atuação, que varia entre nacional e estadual.
articles.body:
Deputados federais e estaduais têm um papel importante em decisões que afetam diretamente o dia a dia da população. Os dois cargos fazem parte do Poder Legislativo e têm a função de discutir e votar projetos de lei e fiscalizar o governo. A principal diferença está no alcance dessa atuação.

📍Em uma série de 50 vídeos, o g1 vai explicar os principais temas das eleições de 2026. Os conteúdos mostram como funcionam as pesquisas, explicam o papel dos cargos em disputa e o funcionamento do Congresso, e trazem orientações práticas para votar. A série também aborda o impacto das novas tecnologias na campanha, como inteligência artificial, deepfakes e influenciadores.

Enquanto os deputados federais atuam em questões de interesse nacional, na Câmara dos Deputados , em Brasília, os deputados estaduais trabalham nas assembleias legislativas e tratam de assuntos que são de competência dos estados.

Tanto os deputados federais quanto os estaduais e distritais são eleitos para mandatos de quatro anos.

Entre as principais funções dos deputados federais estão participar de mudanças na Constituição, fiscalizar os atos do governo federal e propor, discutir e votar projetos que podem virar leis válidas em todo o país. Temas como regras trabalhistas e impostos, por exemplo, passam pela atuação dos deputados federais.

Deputados federais aprovaram PEC que determina que parlamentares só podem ser processados pelo STF com autorização da Câmara ou do Senado — Foto: Bruno Spada / Câmara dos Deputados

Os deputados federais podem ainda fiscalizar a aplicação de recursos públicos, convocar ministros para prestar esclarecimentos e participar de comissões que investigam determinados assuntos, conhecidas como CPIs.

A Câmara dos Deputados é formada por 513 deputados federais. Cada estado e o Distrito Federal elegem no mínimo 8 e no máximo 70 deputados federais. Essa distribuição leva em consideração a população de cada unidade da federação.

O deputado estadual exerce uma função semelhante a do deputado federal, mas sua atuação é restrita ao estado pelo qual foi eleito. Esses parlamentares trabalham nas assembleias legislativas estaduais.

Entre suas principais atribuições estão propor, discutir e votar projetos de lei estaduais e fiscalizar o governo do estado. Eles também têm a responsabilidade de fiscalizar os atos do governador e a utilização dos recursos públicos estaduais.

Deputados estaduais na Assembleia Legislativa do Rio Grande do Norte. — Foto: ALRN/Divulgação

No Distrito Federal, a estrutura é diferente. Em vez de deputados estaduais, os eleitores escolhem deputados distritais, que exercem funções legislativas relacionadas às competências que o Distrito Federal acumula de estado e município.

O número de deputados estaduais varia de um estado para outro e está relacionado ao tamanho da representação de cada unidade da federação na Câmara dos Deputados. O Acre, por exemplo, tem 24 deputados estaduais, enquanto São Paulo tem 94.

articles.title: Relatos de violência, acolhimento e orientação marcam rotina das atendentes do Ligue 180 | G1
articles.standfirst: Profissionais da central relatam casos de cárcere privado, violência familiar e medo das vítimas. Serviço registra mais de 1 milhão de atendimentos nos primeiros sete meses de 2026.
articles.summary: Profissionais da central relatam casos de cárcere privado, violência familiar e medo das vítimas. Serviço registra mais de 1 milhão de atendimentos nos primeiros sete meses de 2026.
articles.body:
A Central de Atendimento às Mulheres (Ligue 180), em Brasília, recebe diariamente ligações de mulheres em situação de violência que buscam orientação, acolhimento ou apoio para denunciar agressões. Do outro lado da linha, o trabalho das atendentes contraria o ditado popular "em briga de marido e mulher não se mete a colher" para acolher e orientar mulheres vítimas de violência. (Veja abaixo como pedir ajuda).

O g1 foi até a central para mostrar a rotina de atendentes que estão do outro lado da linha e ajudam mulheres que procuram o serviço em busca de informação, orientação ou para denunciar uma situação de violência.

“Alguns relatos tocam a gente. Não tem como não tocar. Aqui a gente lida com todo tipo de denúncia. Às vezes ela [a vítima] busca uma informação, ou só quer desabafar, ou quer contar o que está acontecendo”, contou uma atendente que não quis ter a identidade revelada.

🔎 O Ligue 180, gerenciado pelo Ministério das Mulheres, é um serviço de utilidade pública que acolhe mulheres e orienta sobre direitos, serviços e políticas públicas. Nos sete primeiros meses deste ano, a central registrou mais de um milhão de atendimentos nos primeiros sete meses deste ano.

Outra colaboradora resumiu o sentimento de ajudar as mulheres como “satisfação e dever cumprido”.

“A partir do momento que ela faz a primeira ligação aqui, a gente já sente que ela tá criando coragem de denunciar. A sensação é satisfação e dever cumprido”, relata.

A central reúne cerca de 370 profissionais, entre atendentes, psicólogas, gestoras e capacitadoras. As equipes recebem acompanhamento psicológico semanal, individual ou coletivo, para lidar com o impacto emocional dos relatos de violência ouvidos diariamente.

Apesar da sensação de gratificação por ajudar vítimas, a rotina na central também é marcada por situações difíceis.

Uma das atendentes lembrou o caso de uma mulher mantida em cárcere privado pelo companheiro e sem apoio da própria família.

“Teve uma situação de uma moça que não tinha apoio nenhum da família. Os pais achavam que ela apanhava porque ela merecia. O marido mantinha em cárcere privado. Ela me ligou escondida. Era usuário de drogas e alcoólatra. Ela conseguiu registrar, graças a Deus, a denúncia aqui, porque ela não tinha nem como ir para a cidade”, disse uma das atendentes.

Em outro atendimento, quem procurou ajuda foi uma criança.

"Outra situação foi de uma criança de 10 anos. Ele telefonou para contar o que estava acontecendo com a mãe dele. Estava muito nervoso e com muito medo de que algo pior acontecesse", afirmou.

Uma atendente também contou sobre o caso de uma idosa que sofria violência praticada pelo próprio filho.

“Ela ligou chorando muito, e o agressor dela era o filho. Por um lado, ela não queria registrar a denúncia. Era só ela e o filho. Ela ficou bem dividida. Eu conversei bastante com ela, orientei que poderia buscar apoio psicológico e ela acabou não registrando a denúncia. Mas ficou muito feliz porque pôde, além de receber orientação, desabafar. Ela não tinha ninguém para desabafar”.

“Tem uma história de uma mulher que me ligou, estava nervosa e, no final do atendimento, ela pediu várias vezes para eu acreditar nela e confiar que ela não ia voltar com o agressor. Como se ela precisasse provar”, relatou.

Violência contra a mulher — Foto: © Paulo H. Carvalho/Agência Brasília

Apoio e capacitação psicológica para as atendentes

As profissionais que trabalham na Central de Atendimento às Mulheres recebem acompanhamento psicológico regular para lidar com os impactos da atividade.

Fabiana Emir da Silva, coordenadora de Psicologia e Treinamento da central, explica que a preparação das atendentes busca equilibrar acolhimento e distanciamento profissional.

"O principal aspecto é que a colaboradora precisa unir a fala com a escuta, na empatia, mas também fazer uma separação, para não transferir esses sentimentos para ela mesma e conseguir fazer um atendimento imparcial, de uma forma que essa demandante consiga se sentir livre o suficiente para contar o que aconteceu", disse a coordenadora.

Segundo a coordenadora, as profissionais também são treinadas para evitar a revitimização das mulheres durante os atendimentos.

“Às vezes, a escuta vai se somando e se reestruturando nessa criação para que ela continue a contar aquilo que aconteceu a ela de uma maneira que não seja revitimizada”.

O acompanhamento psicológico acontece uma vez por semana, por cerca de uma hora e meia, e também pode ser acionado individualmente em situações de crise.

“Nós também atuamos com apoio individual, porque pode acontecer de a colaboradora ter uma desestabilização durante esse atendimento. Toda a parte da psicologia está aqui para atuar não só no pós-atendimento, mas também durante o atendimento e nessa prevenção”, afirmou.

Nos sete primeiros meses de 2026, o Ligue 180 registrou mais de um milhão de atendimentos. Número que corresponde a 95% de todo o volume registrado no ano passado.

Segundo dados do Ministério das Mulheres, entre 1º de janeiro e 31 de julho de 2026, foram realizados 1.035.647 atendimentos, uma média de 4.884 por dia.

Para Estela Bezerra, secretária Nacional de Enfrentamento à Violência contra as Mulheres do Ministério das Mulheres, o aumento está relacionado principalmente à maior confiança no serviço e ao conhecimento sobre o Ligue 180.

“Nem sempre quem chama é a mulher vítima. Às vezes, é uma irmã, uma vizinha, uma amiga, uma filha ou um filho. Esse aumento significa que as mulheres estão tendo confiança e conhecimento do Ligue 180. Mas também pode significar que esse debate está motivando as mulheres a procurar o serviço, já que o tema está sendo pautado por instituições públicas e privadas.”

Segundo ela, o crescimento também pode estar relacionado à maior exposição dos casos de violência contra as mulheres, principalmente por meio de imagens registradas por câmeras de segurança.

O Ligue 180 funciona 24 horas por dia, todos os dias da semana. As atendentes podem receber chamadas em português, espanhol e inglês.

“O Ligue 180 atua para além do registro de denúncias. O serviço também repassa informações, orientações e indica os serviços da rede de proteção disponíveis”, afirma Juliana Costa, diretora da Central de Atendimento do Ligue 180.

Após o registro da denúncia, o caso recebe um número de protocolo e é encaminhado aos órgãos competentes para a apuração criminal na Segurança Pública e no Ministério Público.

O órgão estadual responsável pelas políticas para as mulheres também é notificado.

É possível acompanhar o andamento da denúncia entrando em contato com o Ligue 180. Para isso, é necessário fornecer o CPF da pessoa denunciante ou o número do protocolo de atendimento.

“Mesmo com medo, as mulheres devem procurar ajuda, porque tem uma saída para a situação de violência e é muito importante que o primeiro passo seja dado para que ela saia desse ciclo”, finaliza uma atendente.

articles.title: Mississippi mayor argues aginst lowering flag for Dolly Parton after her death
articles.summary: Olive Branch, Mississippi, Mayor Ken Adams argues against lowering the flag to half-staff for Dolly Parton, saying the honor should be reserved.
articles.body: A mayor of a small city in Mississippi is arguing against lowering the flag to honor Dolly Parton, worrying that it would "lessen the meaning of the gesture" in the future. "I believe lowering the American flag to half-staff should mean something very significant," Olive Branch, Mississippi, Mayor Ken Adams wrote on the city’s Facebook page on Friday. "In my opinion, it should be reserved for our military heroes, fallen first responders, presidents and other major national leaders, or events that have had a tremendous impact on our country." He added, "If we lower the flag every time a well-known or beloved person passes away, I believe we eventually lessen the meaning of the gesture." DOLLY PARTON'S LIFE IN HER OWN WORDS: FROM SMOKY MOUNTAINS POVERTY TO COUNTRY MUSIC IMMORTALITY Adams began his post by acknowledging the "9 to 5" songstress as a "great person" who "brought happiness to millions of people and has done tremendous things for others throughout her life." He said he had "nothing but respect for her." SHERRILL RIPPED AFTER NEW JERSEY SKIPS FLAG DIRECTIVE HONORING GRAHAM: ‘MOST POLITICAL GOVERNOR’ Adams went on to say that while he doesn’t believe local governments should disregard the president or the governor, Mississippi operates under "Home Rule," which he said gives local governments broad discretion. Both President Donald Trump and Mississippi Gov. Tate Reeves ordered U.S. and state flags to be flown at half-staff for one week after her death at 80 years old on Tuesday. DOLLY PARTON REFUSED TO PICK POLITICAL SIDES FOR DECADES: ‘I’M NOT IN POLITICS, I’M AN ENTERTAINER’ "The President can make the decision for the country. The Governor can make the decision for the State of Mississippi. I believe a mayor should have the ability to make a decision for his or her city," Adams continued. "I also don’t believe residents elected me to be a ‘salute and execute’ Mayor but to lead with conviction." He stressed that his decision wasn’t about "disrespecting Dolly Parton. It isn’t about politics. And it certainly isn’t about saying she wasn’t a great American." DOLLY PARTON'S BELOVED LITERACY MISSION SEES SURGE OF SUPPORT AFTER COUNTRY ICON'S DEATH "It’s simply my belief that the American flag at half-staff is one of the highest honors we can give, and I believe that honor should be reserved for truly extraordinary circumstances," he said. "Sometimes preserving the meaning of an honor means being selective about when we use it." Adams faced criticism in the comments, with one person writing, "She did more for children than any politician ever has. That should raise her status in your eyes from ‘just a celebrity.’" BROADCAST BIAS: DOLLY PARTON TAUGHT THE WORLD THE WAY TO BE UNIVERSALLY BELOVED "I’d lower it for Dolly before any politician," a second person stated. A third commenter wrote: "When you said 'it's simply my belief', I guess you said it all. Doesn't matter to you what the President, the Governor or your residents believe. And 'reserved for people who made a tremendous impact?' Well...she was probably the most unifying figure of the past 40 years; and she donated 325 million books to kids. Sounds like an impact." A fourth person who said they were a veteran and first responder wrote that they were "100% ok with lowering the flags for Dolly. She gave her time and money to the military and multiply organizations. She earned this." articles.title: El-Sayed apologizes to Jewish Democrats for synagogue attack comment
articles.summary: Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed apologized Saturday for comments he made following an attack on a Detroit-area synagogue earlier this year, as he seeks to ease concerns among Jewish voters ahead of the November election. “I made a mistake,” El-Sayed said during an appearance before the Michigan Democratic Jewish Caucus at the state party’s…
articles.body:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed apologized Saturday for comments he made following an attack on a Detroit-area synagogue earlier this year, as he seeks to ease concerns among Jewish voters ahead of the November election.

“I made a mistake,” El-Sayed said during an appearance before the Michigan Democratic Jewish Caucus at the state party’s convention in Lansing on Saturday. “I should have issued a statement, of course condemning it, and it just should have been the full stop.”

El-Sayed was referring to his response to a March attack on Temple Israel in West Bloomfield Township in Michigan, where authorities say a man intentionally drove a truck into the synagogue and injured a security guard to deliberately target Jewish people.

In his initial response, El-Sayed said there was “never a justification for attacking innocent people,” but also said “violence is a cycle,” and used the phrase “hurt people hurt people.”

According to authorities, the attacker, a naturalized U.S. citizen from Lebanon, had lost family members in an Israeli attack in Lebanon earlier that month.

El-Sayed told the group of Jewish Democrats on Saturday that he had been trying to provide broader context but acknowledged that doing so in the immediate aftermath of the attack was a mistake.

“If my statement caused pain, I’m sorry,” he said. “That was not what I intended.”

El-Sayed has faced broader scrutiny over his stance on Israel and Gaza, as well as his relationship with political commentators that are critical of Israel.

He distanced himself from left-wing streamer Hasan Piker, who joined him on the campaign trail during the Democratic primary, drew outrage from a slate of Democratic lawmakers over Piker’s comments about American Jews supporting Israel.

Piker said that if American Jews continue promoting the idea that they are “singularly invested in Israel,” someone could eventually “take action” against American Jews.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) called the remarks “dangerous and antisemitic,” while El-Sayed said he has “no plans” to campaign with Piker during the general election.

articles.title: Tucker Carlson: Trump needs to be removed from office ‘immediately’
articles.summary: Conservative podcaster Tucker Carlson said Friday that President Trump should be removed from office if he is considering using nuclear weapons first, saying even entertaining the possibility should disqualify a president from serving. “The second any president actively considers the first use of nuclear weapons, that person should be removed from office immediately, because that’s…
articles.body:
Conservative podcaster Tucker Carlson said Friday that President Trump should be removed from office if he is considering using nuclear weapons first, saying even entertaining the possibility should disqualify a president from serving.

“The second any president actively considers the first use of nuclear weapons, that person should be removed from office immediately, because that’s got to be the red line, destroying all of humanity with a nuclear strike,” Carlson said.

Carlson made the comments during a conversation with Joe Kent, the former director of the National Counterterrorism Center who resigned earlier this year in opposition to the war with Iran.

Carlson, who noted that he strongly opposed both efforts to impeach Trump during his first term, questioned why the same standard would not apply if a president were weighing a nuclear first strike.

“Why isn’t there an attempt to remove him from office, like, immediately?” Carlson said. “Anyone who would even tolerate that kind of talk from any of his subordinates or employees is by definition unfit.”

Trump has not publicly said he is considering using a nuclear weapon first.

Carlson’s comments come as he raised concerns about both the administration’s approach to Iran and a nuclear strategy being developed at the Pentagon.

Earlier this month, Under Secretary of Defense for policy Elbridge Colby said at a conference that officials are looking to give the president and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth “credible, rational nuclear options.”

Kent said he was concerned about where the administration could turn if conventional military options fail to get the outcome Trump wants in Iran.

“I think we would be fools to think that this couldn’t happen here in this current scenario, especially as the administration scrambles for a way out,” he said.

Trump and Carlson, who was once an ally of the MAGA movement and of Trump, have clashed in recent months over their opposing views on foreign policy, with Carlson being a vocal opponent of the Iran war.

Trump last week bashed Carlson on Truth Social, calling him a “loser” for meeting with Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) and former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-Ga.).

articles.title: Minnesota Supreme Court rejects Mike Lindell’s bid to recount GOP gubernatorial primary
articles.summary: MyPillow founder Mike Lindell has long denied President Donald Trump’s loss in the 2020 presidential election.
articles.body: MyPillow founder Mike Lindell has long denied President Donald Trump’s loss in the 2020 presidential election. Now, he’s refusing to accept his own election loss in the GOP primary for governor of Minnesota. The Minnesota Supreme Court rejected Lindell’s bid Saturday to order a full recount of his Aug. 11 loss to state House Speaker Lisa Demuth after she won the Republican primary by 45,000 votes. Chief Justice Natalie E. Hudson wrote in a six-page ruling that the Minnesota secretary of state’s office and its State Canvassing Board provided a recount plan that follows the law and are “not committing any wrongful act, omission, or error” as Lindell claimed. Lindell told NBC News in a phone call Saturday evening that he plans to appeal the ruling to the U.S. Supreme Court. He said that his team is also requesting the data from all 87 counties through the Freedom of Information Act in order to pursue an independent investigation of the election data. “I’m willing to pay even more money. I don’t care what it costs,” Lindell said. Lindell previously pledged to pay an estimated $825,000 to cover a full hand recount and audit of the race but refused to pay the money on Monday, which marked the state’s deadline, after finding out that the recount only included counting the ballots cast for either Lindell or Demuth. Lindell sued the Minnesota secretary of state’s office and its State Canvassing Board Monday, claiming that they pulled a “bait-and-switch” on him by not counting the ballots for everyone in the seven-candidate Republican field. The secretary of state’s office said in a statement Tuesday that it provided the contingent recount plan to Lindell after the State Canvassing Board approved it Aug. 18, writing that “the plan follows state law and administrative rules on recount procedures and is consistent with previous recount plans.” Hudson acknowledged in her ruling that Lindell argued that “he is entitled to a full recount for both the Democratic and Republican primary races for governor ‘to ensure that there are no anomalies in the ballots, whether the votes cast are for the Democratic or Republican primaries,’ and that this recount must include ‘the recording of votes for every candidate.’” “But Lindell’s focus on alleged anomalies confuses the purpose of a manual recount with an election contest,” Hudson wrote. Hudson maintained that the recount plan approved by the canvassing board Aug. 18 follows protocol, stating that during the recount the ballots would first be sorted between those cast for the Democratic or Republican primary and then the Republican ballots would be separated into three piles: one for Lindell, one for Demuth and one for all other candidates. “In other words, after all votes are sorted and counted, Lindell would know whether he is the winner over Demuth,” Hudson wrote. “And all ballots, in all piles, would be counted and subject to challenge.” Hudson’s ruling backs up Demuth’s victory in the GOP primary, reinforcing her spot in the general election against Democratic nominee, Sen. Amy Klobuchar. Lindell said Saturday he would not be satisfied with anything less than a full hand recount of all ballots cast in the Minnesota gubernatorial primary races, arguing that there were “anomalies” in the election data due to the use of electronic voting machines. Before his own gubernatorial campaign, Lindell faced multiple lawsuits after he repeated debunked claims that the 2020 election was rigged by voting machines. Lindell was found to have defamed a former employee of one company, Dominion Voting Systems, in June 2025. Lindell has denied the claim. In another defamation case, Lindell has refused to pay $56,369 in sanctions to voting machine company Smartmatic USA Corp. Because he still has not paid what the court ordered, Lindell now owes even more than the original sanctions in court fees. He told NBC News this month that he still does not intend to pay either the fees or sanctions.

articles.title: IDF general warns talks with Hamas, Hezbollah lack a clear strategy for victory
articles.summary: "I don't know if we're being played or if a false reality is being manufactured. but in this false narrative, we're pretending to run a process that will ult...
articles.body:
"I don't know if we're being played or if a false reality is being manufactured... but in this false narrative, we're pretending to run a process that will ultimately disarm Hamas."

The diplomatic efforts underway between Israel and Gaza and Lebanon "are largely ineffective... half-baked in terms of what we will actually achieve," Brig.-Gen. (res.) Oren Avman told 103FM on Friday.

Avman, who is a former commander of the Kfir Brigade, made these comments when weighing in on a recent report that said Prime Minister Netanyahu permitted former Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar to maintain direct contact with Hamas officials during the war.

He added, "I don't know if we're being played or if a false reality is being manufactured - on top of the state's overall conduct, which already draws plenty of valid criticism - but in this false narrative, we're pretending to run a process that will ultimately disarm Hamas."

Avman noted further: "Over the last generation, state entities have virtually ceased to exist in our strategic reality. We have to recognize that - it's been the case for over 25 years."

Despite his criticism, Avman emphasized that he does not reject diplomacy itself. "Diplomatic efforts and dialogue are always vital and must continue regardless. The real question is where they ultimately lead and whether we are being forced to compromise on essentials," he said.

"The diplomatic efforts of 2026 must persist. We are in a completely different era. Over the last generation, we negotiated with Arafat and the Palestinian Authority, reached understandings with Hezbollah following Operations Accountability and Grapes of Wrath as well as the Second Lebanon War, and now, in one way or another, we are pursuing understandings with Hamas."

'When human lives are on the line, it's legitimate to negotiate with the devil'

Avman's skepticism of the diplomatic process stopped short of criticizing the diplomatic process when it comes to the lives of hostages.

"When saving human lives is on the line, especially regarding the hostages following our terrible failure on October 7 - it is legitimate to negotiate even with the devil," he said.

"As long as we succeed in bringing them home safely, you make deals with enemies, not friends, just like prisoner exchanges between sovereign states. That's why I draw a clear line between an operation aimed at saving lives, like the hostage situation, and all these recent reports about talks before and after, funding, Qatar, and the like."

'The IDF in Lebanon is like Home Alone 2'

Turning to the Lebanese front, Avman sharply criticized the lack of a clear political objective. "Regarding the talks on Lebanon, the IDF finds itself in a 'Home Alone 2' situation - full of holes like Swiss cheese, operating without a clear political compass while locked in localized battles of attrition," he said.

"The question is whether we're stuck in a game of ping-pong - they launch a drone, we scramble F-16s or hit back somehow. The IDF is bogged down in a security zone, and when it comes to dealing with Hezbollah, the problem is that reality is dictating our actions instead of us shaping reality."

In closing, Avman highlighted two core issues that he believes plague Israel across all fronts.

"Looking at all fronts, there are two underlying drivers. One is decision-making paralysis, and the second, highly problematic driver is the immense strain on the IDF , coupled with a complete lack of grasp of the reality facing reserve, career, and active-duty soldiers. Managing these two factors simultaneously makes this an extraordinarily complex situation."

articles.title: Iceland votes on resuming EU membership talks as Trump's push for neighboring Greenland looms over debate
articles.summary: President Donald Trump's push to acquire Greenland added a new security dimension to Iceland's EU referendum, with 275,000 eligible voters weighing in.
articles.body: Icelanders voted Saturday on whether to reopen negotiations to join the European Union, with President Donald Trump's push for U.S. control of neighboring Greenland adding a new security dimension to a debate that has divided the NATO ally for years. Iceland, strategically positioned in the North Atlantic and roughly 180 miles from Greenland, has no military of its own and relies on NATO and a longstanding defense agreement with the United States for its security, according to RTE and The Associated Press. Trump's repeated interest in acquiring Greenland has unsettled some Icelanders and raised questions about whether closer ties with the EU could provide another layer of security for the island nation, the AP reported. TRUMP SAYS NATO FAILED TWO KEY TESTS DURING HIGH-STAKES TURKEY SUMMIT: 'NOT HAPPY' Roughly 275,000 eligible voters were asked whether Iceland should resume membership negotiations with the EU. As of Saturday evening, the result had not been officially called. If the referendum passes, Iceland would resume negotiations with the EU, followed by another referendum on actual membership, RTE reported. Iceland's government, led by Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir, has vowed to respect the result, although the referendum is technically nonbinding. "This has been a tight race, extremely exciting," Frostadóttir said after voting Saturday. She said the campaign had "lifted discussions about the EU, about Iceland's place in the world, about our general geopolitical situation and status, to a higher level." While domestic and economic issues have played a central role in the referendum campaign, Trump's ambitions for neighboring Greenland have also cast a shadow over Iceland's debate about its place in Europe and the broader geopolitical landscape. TRUMP ARRIVES AT NATO SUMMIT AS IRAN RIFT LOOMS ABOVE ALLIANCE TALKS Trump has repeatedly expressed interest in acquiring Greenland, a self-governing Danish territory, previously saying the U.S. would obtain the strategically important Arctic island "one way or the other." The Trump administration has also previously weighed options for acquiring Greenland, including the potential use of military force. Such a move against territory belonging to Denmark, a fellow NATO member, would pose an extraordinary challenge to the alliance and its collective-defense commitments. Trump has also mistakenly referred to Iceland while discussing Greenland on multiple occasions, according to the AP. Iceland itself was drawn into the discussion earlier this year after former Rep. Billy Long, who is now Trump's ambassador to Iceland, apologized for privately joking to House lawmakers that the country could become the "52nd state" with him as its governor. articles.title: Survey: Most believe Germany would be harmed if AfD enters government
articles.summary: Nearly half of Germans believe the inclusion of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party in a federal government would be harmful to the country, ac...
articles.body:
Nearly half of Germans believe the inclusion of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party in a federal government would be harmful to the country, according to a survey by opinion research institute Insa.

The survey found 47% agreed with the statement that Germany would be harmed if the AfD came to power, while 36% disagreed. Of those surveyed, 17% did not provide an answer.

The survey, commissioned by the Sunday edition of tabloid Bild and published a week ahead of crucial state elections, found 22% of respondents said they would leave Germany if the AfD came to power.

A total of 1,001 respondents across Germany took part in the survey between August 27-28.

The AfD, Germany's largest opposition party, was founded in 2013 as an anti-euro party then shifted direction to focus on reducing migration.

The AfD branches in five of Germany's 16 federal states - including four states in the east - are classified as "confirmed" right-wing extremist movements by intelligence agencies, allowing for the party to be monitored by authorities.

The party has risen in popularity recently, benefiting from discontent with the political establishment in Berlin.

The AfD is polling above 40% in Saxony-Anhalt ahead of a crucial state election on September 6, raising the prospect that it could achieve an outright majority - provoking intense debate as to what that might mean for the country as a whole.

All mainstream parties refuse to work with the AfD, a policy famously known as the "firewall," but successive governments have rejected calls for the party to be banned due to its extremist positions.

articles.standfirst: El Ministro de Transporte replica a las críticas por su gestión con Ryanair
articles.summary: El Ministro de Transporte replica a las críticas por su gestión con Ryanair
articles.body: Óscar Puente ha respondido con dureza a las críticas del economista José Carlos Díez sobre su gestión de las operaciones de Ryanair en España. "Lo que le jode a Óscar Puente es que por negarse a negociar ha dejado sin vuelos el aeropuerto de Valladolid y quiere volver a ser alcalde", ha comentado en redes sociales. Además, ha publicado una cifra de pasajeros en Valladolid, 209.000 en 2023 y 87.500 en 2025. "Sólo piensan en seguir subidos al coche oficial", ha rematado en sus redes sociales. La respuesta del ministro de Transportes no ha tardado en llegar. "Eres tontísimo, muchacho. Ryanair se fue y vino Vueling. A Rey muerto, Rey puesto. Y el volumen de viajeros se recuperó", ha explicado el dirigente del PSOE en su cuenta personal de X, antes Twitter. Óscar Puente también ha lanzado otro dardo contundente: "A ti lo que te jode es que no cedamos al chantaje de quienes pretenden gobernar sin presentarse a las elecciones". El titular de Transportes ha acompañado su publicación en redes sociales con capturas de varios artículos que respaldan sus datos. En uno de ellos, del Diario de Valladolid, podemos leer el siguiente titular: 'Vueling recuperará el vuelo a Barcelona desde Valladolid abandonado por Ryanair'. En el siguiente, de la web de Aena, se destaca al crecimiento de los vuelos: 'Crece un 49,4 por ciento el tráfico de pasajeros en el Aeropuerto de Valladolid en el mes de julio'. Según esta última información, en el primer semestre del año 2026 las instalaciones sumaron 62.589 pasajeros. El conflicto de Óscar Puente con Ryanair viene de lejos. La semana pasada, el político y el CEO de la aerolínea, Michael O'Leary, mantuvieron un sonado pulso a través de las redes sociales. Este último afirmó que el ministro no sabía sumar y el titular de Transportes le respondió de forma tajante: "Ya sabes: si no te gustan nuestras reglas vuela a otro sitio".

articles.title: Minnesota high court rejects Lindell’s gubernatorial primary recount bid
articles.summary: The Minnesota Supreme Court on Saturday rejected MyPillow founder Mike Lindell’s (R) bid for a recount of the state’s gubernatorial primary election, effectively confirming an 11-point loss that he has defiantly challenged. Chief Justice Natalie E. Hudson wrote in a six-page ruling that Lindell’s “claim fails on the merits.” “Lindell argues that he is entitled…
articles.body:
The Minnesota Supreme Court on Saturday rejected MyPillow founder Mike Lindell’s (R) bid for a recount of the state’s gubernatorial primary election, effectively confirming an 11-point loss that he has defiantly challenged.

Chief Justice Natalie E. Hudson wrote in a six-page ruling that Lindell’s “claim fails on the merits.”

“Lindell argues that he is entitled to a full recount for both the Democratic and Republican primary races for governor ‘to ensure that there are no anomalies in the ballots, whether the votes cast are for the Democratic or Republican primaries,’ and that this recount must include ‘the recording of votes for every candidate,'” she wrote.

“But Lindell’s focus on alleged anomalies confused the purpose of a manual recount with an election contest,” she added, before citing legal precedent.

Hudson also wrote that the Minnesota secretary of state’s office and the State Canvassing Board were “not committing any wrongful act, omission, or error by following –– as the Secretary of State proposes –– the procedures set forth” in state election law.

Lindell called for a recount after his primary loss to state House Speaker Lisa Demuth (R), who won the Aug. 11 primary by 45,000 votes.

He told NBC News on Saturday that he plans to appeal the ruling, adding that his team requested election data from all 87 counties through the Freedom of Information Act to conduct an independent investigation of that data.

“I’m willing to pay even more money,” Lindell told the outlet, having previously said he’ll cover a full recount with an estimated $825,000. “I don’t care what it costs.”

Lindell refused to pay the money last Monday, the state’s deadline for a recount and audit of the race, after the recount would have solely been about counting the ballots cast for him or Demuth.

Hudson wrote that Lindell, having missed the Monday deadline, “instead sent documentation to the Secretary of State to reflect wire transfer readiness, and he filed this section 204B.44 petition.”

That same day, Lindell said he would file a temporary restraining order against Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon, claiming that Simon’s office had put Lindell “in an untenable position” by placing restrictions on his proposed audit by limiting the recount to Lindell and Demuth.

Lindell’s campaign previously told The Hill on Monday that “anomalies … identified by Mike Lindell’s team show an algorithm that applies to ALL of the candidates not simply Lindell and Demuth.”

The MyPillow founder currently owes the electronic voting system company Smartmatic $56,369 in sanctions following a defamation lawsuit, which one that his attorneys says he cannot afford. Lindell has accused the company in several media appearances of rigging the 2020 presidential election, echoing similar false claims made by President Trump, who endorsed Lindell in his race against Demuth.

articles.title: What happens when Republican senators have nothing left to lose? Not much.
articles.summary: Often called the “Wounded Bear” or YOLO (“you only live once”) Caucus, these lawmakers have nothing to lose. But despite a greater willingness to voice objections to Trump nominations and policies, they almost never vote “no” when it counts.
articles.body:
For years, we have been told that Republican senators privately object to many of President Trump’s policies and appointments but do not resist because Republican voters would punish them at the ballot box. There are at least four senators who have little to fear from elections or Trump right now, yet remarkably little has changed.

Sen. Mitch McConnell (R-Ky.) is retiring in January. Sens. Bill Cassidy (R-La.) and John Cornyn (R-Texas) both lost primaries to Trump-backed opponents and will not run again. And Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) opted against seeking reelection after Trump threatened to support a primary challenger against him.

Often called the “ Wounded Bear ” or YOLO (“you only live once”) caucus, these lawmakers have nothing to lose. But despite a greater willingness to voice objections to Trump nominations and policies, they almost never vote “no” when it counts.

Trump’s recent nomination of Todd Blanche to be attorney general illustrates the pattern.

Cornyn and Tillis demanded a written commitment ending Trump’s proposed $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund as the price for their support. Neither focused much on the provisions granting Trump and his family immunity from IRS investigations. Widely denounced as a slush fund to reward Trump allies and supporters — including potentially rioters who attacked Capitol police on Jan. 6, 2021 — it was labeled by Cornyn as “politically tone-deaf” and a “payout pot for punks.” Tillis called it “ stupid on stilts ;” McConnell declared it “ utterly stupid , morally wrong.” Cassidy accused Blanche of showing “ poor judgment ” in helping negotiate it, questioned his independence, and expressed concern about the Justice Department’s “bringing suits against political enemies.”

Every Democrat, along with Republicans Susan Collins (Maine) and Lisa Murkowski (Alaska), opposed Blanche. One more “no” vote would have killed the nomination. Hospitalized and unable to vote, McConnell did not take a public position. Cornyn and Tillis voted yes, after Blanche ordered the Justice Department to rescind the fund — an order that can easily be reversed , as Trump has suggested he might do.

With the nomination hanging in the balance, Cassidy put it over the top , holding back tears as he explained that an acting attorney general might be even worse than Blanche.

All four appear no more willing to sink a Cabinet-level nomination, block a major Trump initiative, or defend the Senate’s institutional role now than they were before.

McConnell voted against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, former Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard, and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., as well as Trump’s Canadian tariff and global tariff “emergencies.” As he surely expected, none of his votes changed the outcome.

Cornyn almost never opposed Trump before losing his primary. After losing, Cornyn blocked two controversial ambassadorial nominees for the Foreign Relations Committee, but let them advance after getting “assurances” on AIDS funding.

A member of the Judiciary Committee, Tillis blocked the nomination of Ed Martin to serve as the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia in 2025 because of his comments about the January 6 attack on the Capitol. After deciding not to run again, Tillis delayed (but did not stop) the nomination of Kevin Warsh as Federal Reserve chair, until the Justice Department dropped its criminal investigation of then-Chair Jerome Powell.

Before losing his primary, Cassidy, a physician and chair of the congressional committee overseeing public health, helped block the nomination of Casey Means for surgeon general. But after expressing grave doubts about RFK Jr.’s views on vaccines, he still cast the decisive vote to confirm him as Secretary of Health and Human Services.

After losing his primary, Cassidy declined to schedule hearings on Heidi Overton’s nomination to head the Food and Drug Administration, calling her support for Trump’s executive order on vaccines “almost disqualifying.” Cassidy also joined Democrats in trying to block Bill Pulte’s nomination for acting Director of National Intelligence, an effort that failed in a 49-49 tie.

But Cassidy folded on Blanche’s nomination. And after initially supporting a war powers resolution to block further military action in Iran, Cassidy backed down after receiving a briefing he had demanded in a heated confrontation with Trump.

In short, whether it involves Trump’s willingness to wage war without congressional approval, appoint his former criminal defense attorney to head an already politicized Justice Department, withhold or redirect funds appropriated by Congress , or demand confirmation of dozens of nominees en bloc , the wounded bears have largely acquiesced.

And why not add Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) to the list? The dean of the Senate , Grassley has championed government oversight of waste, misconduct and abuse by whistleblowers and inspectors general who, he claims, should be “ almost wholly free of supervision .” Nonetheless, when Trump removed 18 inspectors general in January 2025, Grassley sent only a letter of concern , which was not even answered for eight months. He did not employ his signature tactic, holding up nominees for other offices, to ensure the watchdogs would be protected. When his current term ends in 2028, Grassley will be 94. We wonder what accounts for his muted response.

In a closely divided Senate, the YOLOs have enormous leverage, but they are not using it to challenge executive branch overreach. No doubt party loyalty, relationships with Republican colleagues, and a reluctance to help Democrats still matter to them. But it should be deeply troubling that compliance seems to have become Republicans’ default setting.

If senators with nothing to lose won’t insist on preserving the Constitution’s checks, balances and separation of powers, who will?

David Wippman is emeritus president of Hamilton College. Glenn C. Altschuler is the Thomas and Dorothy Litwin Emeritus Professor of American Studies at Cornell University.

articles.title: Why we should bring back the draft
articles.summary: University of Pennsylvania professor Jonathan Zimmerman argues that reinstating a military draft would encourage student activism against the ongoing war in Iran and ensure a more equitable distribution of national defense responsibilities.
articles.body:
Last week, as the war in Iran neared its six-month mark, President Trump said it would “ continue for as long as necessary. ” More than 750 American service members have been killed or wounded since the U.S. attacked Iran on Feb. 28. That is a tiny number compared to the Iranian casualty toll, which has topped 37,000 .

Our college campuses are silent . That’s not just because universities clamped down on protests following the burst of anti-Israel demonstrations in 2023 and 2024. It is also because our students know they won’t be sent to fight in the Middle East.

That is precisely why we need a military draft. Our colleges would explode with protest, just they did during America’s war in Vietnam. Everyone would learn more about the conflict in Iran. And maybe, just maybe, we could convince our leaders to end it.

Most students in the Vietnam era received draft deferments, which is why college attendance shot up . So did grade inflation : sympathetic professors knew that students could be conscripted if they flunked out, so they gave fewer D’s and F’s.

Student draft deferments ended in 1971 , except for people training in medicine and divinity. From the start of the war, though, every male student knew they could be drafted once they got their degree.

So college campuses were cauldrons of protest. At the University of Pennsylvania — where I teach — students staged a seven-hour sit-in in 1967 to condemn on-campus recruiting by Dow Chemical, which produced the napalm that killed and mutilated so many people in Vietnam. Three years later, when National Guardsmen gunned down four students at Kent State, 1,300 colleges and universities witnessed protests and 500 closed because of student and faculty strikes.

But I haven’t heard a peep of antiwar sentiment as students return this semester. They stride happily across our verdant quads, chatting about classes and internships and hookups.

I don’t know how many of them are aware of the proposed new speech restrictions at Penn, which ban “disruptive” protest (without defining that) and any demonstration where “health and safety is endangered” (ditto). But here’s what I do know: if there was a military draft, the restrictions wouldn’t matter. Students would raise their voices, ignoring our efforts to silence them.

And here’s another thing I know: a truly universal draft would make the United States a more equitable place. But the Vietnam-era draft was far from universal or equitable.

That’s because people with money and power could evade it. After receiving four student deferments, Trump obtained a medical exemption when a podiatrist — who was also a tenant of Trump’s father — certified that Trump had bone spurs in his heels.

George W. Bush’s father — in Congress at the time — reportedly pulled strings to get his son into a National Guard unit, which let members fulfill their military duty without going to Vietnam. Bill Clinton got a deferment during his Rhodes Scholarship in England and then told his local draft board that he was “too well educated” to serve as a soldier, the board’s secretary recalled .

Sadly, Clinton was correct. The war was fought mostly by working-class Americans without college degrees, who didn’t have the means or connections to buy their way out.

And in a democracy, the burden of national defense should be shared. That’s why Sen. Edward Kennedy (D-Mass.) and Rep. Charles Rangel (D-N.Y.) — two of the most liberal members of Congress — objected when Richard Nixon ended the draft in 1973. As Kennedy argued , an all-volunteer army would result in “poor people fighting a rich man’s war.” Rangel proposed a bill that would have required all Americans between 18 and 25 to serve for two years, either in the military or in a civilian capacity.

If it was truly universal, Rangel noted, the draft would bring together Americans from different backgrounds into a common national project. In a recent interview , likewise, California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) suggested that compulsory national service could “knit this country back together.”

Trump isn’t having it. During the 2024 campaign, he warned — without evidence — that Democratic nominee Kamala Harris would bring back the draft . And when members of his own party — including JD Vance and Lindsey Graham — said they were open to the idea, he shot that down as well .

The Selective Service recently announced a new policy to automatically register eligible men, which fed internet rumors that another draft is imminent. So did comments by the recently departed White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt. Asked about a possible draft, Leavitt said President Trump “keeps his options on the table.”

But he wouldn’t want his own kid to get drafted, of course. That’s the point of the satirical “Draft Barron Trump” website produced by South Park screenwriter Toby Morton, urging Trump’s 20-year-old son to serve in Iran. Right-wing podcaster Theo Von also called on Barron Trump to enlist, noting that “elites and politicians that are leading us into these wars might make different choices if it was their children.”

Students at our colleges might make different choices, too, if their own lives were on the line. They would be storming the ramparts, demanding that our destructive gambit in Iran come to an end. That’s why they should be required to serve in the military. So should everybody else.

Jonathan Zimmerman teaches history and education at the University of Pennsylvania and serves on the advisory council of the Albert Lepage Center for History in the Public Interest .

articles.body:
The liftoff of China’s Chang’e 7 mission to the moon has been delayed into 2027. Ars Technica reports that the Chinese are being vague about the exact reasons for the delay, only suggesting it is due to, adhering to “the principle of proceeding prudently and reliably, and ensuring absolute success.”

The Chinese mission includes an orbiter, a lander, a rover, and a hopper. The orbiter would circle the moon to narrow down a suitable landing site. Then the lander would touch down, deploying the rover and hopper, likely on the rim of the Shackleton Crater to prospect for ice. Ice is all-important as a resource that would support lunar exploration and development.

When it does lift off, this Chinese ship will be the most complex, sophisticated expedition to Earth’s nearest neighbor since the Apollo lunar landings. It is a reminder that NASA and its international and commercial partners are in a space race, with a prize that illuminates the night sky with a promise of riches, knowledge, and international prestige.

While Typhoon Narra likely was a major contributing factor to the delay, the Chinese have not specifically blamed the storm. This suggests that an underlying technical issue or even several issues may exist that has pushed the launch of the Chang’e into 2027.

In any case, the next window opens up in February or March 2027. If the Chinese are not experiencing technical issues regarding the Chang’e — as they did with the recent loss of the Long March 7A — they should be free to exercise a little more transparency. Otherwise, outside observers have to draw their own conclusions in the dark.

The delay does have some implications for the Space Race 2.0 that the Chinese will not like. It suggests that China may not be able to hold on to preannounced schedules, such as their planned 2030 crewed moon landing. As complex as Chang’e is, an attempt to land people on the moon and bring them home safely to the Earth is significantly more complex. A failed robotic landing is one thing. Dead taikonauts are quite another.

During a Senate hearing in September 2025, former NASA Administrator Jim Bridenstine suggested that it was “highly unlikely” that the U.S. would beat China back to the moon. He cited the SpaceX Starship Human Landing System as a reason, which will require multiple refueling flights in low Earth orbit before proceeding to the moon.

Current NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, on the other hand, has expressed confidence that the Artemis IV crewed lunar landing mission will make the 2028 launch time, which would easily beat the Chinese back to the moon, all other things being equal. However, if the Chinese have to delay their crewed lunar landing mission, NASA and its partners will have more time to iron out any problems, especially with the Human Landing System.

In the meantime, the Chinese delay opens up the possibility that Blue Origin’s Blue Moon Mark 1 will steal a march on the Chinese and wind up being the first robotic probe to land on the lunar south pole. The Blue Moon was scheduled to launch this year but was delayed due to the loss of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket during a static fire test in May 2026, which also destroyed the launch pad. Blue Origin thinks it can rebuild the launch pad by the end of 2026 and thus be able to return to flight either late this year or early in 2027.

Space Race 2.0 includes several firsts that both sides are straining to achieve, such as the first robotic probe to the lunar south pole, the first crewed landing in the 21st century, and finally, the first permanent lunar base.

The lunar base is the main prize, especially because of NASA’s plan to create a virtual lunar city of hundreds of square miles in area . Given the security provisions of the Artemis Accords , NASA and its international and commercial partners would be able to deny access to a great deal of lunar resources and real estate to the Chinese.

Of course, the Chinese might try to do the same thing and deny access to its base and environs to everyone else. But China is not a party to the Artemis Accords, so their justification under international law might be tenuous at best.

It is a messy way to handle a return to the moon, but the only way available, considering current geopolitical realities.

Mark Whittington, who writes frequently about space policy, has published a political study of space exploration titled “Why is It So Hard to Go Back to the Moon? ” as well as “ The Moon, Mars and Beyond ” and “ Why is America Going Back to the Moon? ” He blogs at Curmudgeons Corner.
